agent.problem: Most of this stop's choices cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 3, 8, 11, 12 and 13 ask for unrevealed details: what John must measure, whether he must count worshipers, the witnesses' clothing, the fire, shutting the sky and turning water to blood. These discovery questions outnumber the informed guesses.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The question is not self-contained. "There" points back to card 2's answer without naming what John is measuring, so the necessary context disappears with the earlier card.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The walkthrough only says that fire comes out of the witnesses' mouths. It never conveys the rest of verse 5: the fire devours their enemies, and anyone who wants to harm them must be killed. That lethal protection is an important detail, especially before the beast is later able to kill them.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: Papa Dorin says, "I jump half off my gold base," which puts him partly off the base. His base must always come with him, including when he jumps.

rule.text: The gold base is part of him. He can hop, jump and dive face-first into the chocolate chips, but the base always comes with him. He never steps off it or leaves it behind.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the quoted "Come up here.", the sentence beginning "That's all the voice says," and the sentence beginning "And in that hour."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The card uses "Forever and ever" from Revelation 11:15 before telling about the twenty-four elders in Revelation 11:16, but it cites only verse 16. Its range should begin at verse 15.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: This card only repeats "small and great," which card 11 has just covered, and adds a joke. It does not advance the passage or set up the new detail asked about in card 13, so it functions as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

human.problem: The false statement "He will reign for a thousand years" echoes Revelation 20:4-6. Marking it False is accurate for 11:15, but bakers who know Revelation 20 may read it as denying the thousand-year reign. That touches end-times views that differ between denominations.
human.question: Should wrong answers in Revelation avoid using details that appear elsewhere in Revelation and are tied to disputed end-times views, like the thousand years?
